title: Throughput sampling and warmup journal — Feb 12 2026
content:
Meeting: Weekly perf & benchmark sync — focus: throughput sampling strategy and warmup behavior
Date: 2026-02-12
Attendees: Priya Desai (owner), Ethan Park, Marisol Vega, Ravi Iyer, Tom Hsu (observability), Sarah L. (solutions)
Purpose: Capture recent test runs that show a p99 uplift under mixed short+long sequence workloads and agree next steps for deterministic warmup and sampling changes.

Summary of what triggered this run
- After the quant-kernel rollout + small allocator tweak (kernel v2.3.1 deployed 2026-02-09), several internal smoke runs showed stable qps but p99 increased by ~12–18% for mixed workloads (short chat + long context streaming).
- The highest regressions were on instances with warmup disabled and where client-side sampling used a lower initial sample_rate (0.05).

Baseline (pre-rollout) metrics (representative run: baseline-2026-02-02)
- Workload: mixed-chat (70% short seq <= 64 tokens, 30% long seq 1024 tokens)
- Target QPS: 1200 requests/sec (steady-state), token throughput ~210k tokens/sec aggregate
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 latencies: 28ms / 62ms / 114ms
- Baseline token cost: 0.86 token-ms/op (internal metric)

Observed regression run (reg-2026-02-11)
- Same workload generator, same QPS target, 30m run
- Observed p50/p95/p99: 30ms / 68ms / 132ms (p99 +18% vs baseline)
- Notable: cold-start tail (first 90s) contained multiple 300–600ms spikes correlated with eviction/reattach events in the KV cache and a spike in L2 CPU context switches on the host.

Quick hypotheses from triage
1) Reduced sampling and lower pre-warm client priming meant more requests hit the unprimed KV cache path, causing repeated KV priming penalties at scale.
2) Allocator tweak interacts with quant kernels causing periodic stalls at sequence boundaries for long sequences.
3) Autoscaler scale-down windows and instance churn during test windows increased tail latency due to slower node warmup.

Instrumentation / queries used during the investigation
- PromQL (tail summaries):
  sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le)
  topk(5, sum(rate(kv_prime_ops_total[1m])) by (instance))
- Trace capture: sampled 1:200 during the run; traces linked in the GH run artifacts.
- Logs: host metrics showed CPU context-switch spikes at t+23s and t+47s into several warmup windows.

Test matrix executed (short notes)
- A: baseline config + client sample_rate 0.2 + KV-priming enabled on client (warmup requests 50 per instance) — 30m run — p99: 116ms (aligned with baseline)
- B: production-like config (sample_rate 0.05, no client priming) — reproduces regression p99 130–140ms
- C: production config + warmup hook server-side (kv_cache.prepopulate=true) — p99 118ms, but host CPU busy during warmup window
- D: allocator revert (roll back small patch) + prod config — p99 improved to ~120ms; indicates allocator contribution
- E: increased sampler + increased steady-state batching (batch target 32 -> 48) — p50 improved, but p99 unchanged; suggests tail is not batching-limited

Commands / scripts used (for reproducibility)
- Workload generator: k6 script (runs/bench/scripts/mixed_chat.k6.js)
- Example invocation:
  k6 run --vus 400 --duration 30m mixed_chat.k6.js --env TARGET_URL=https://staging-rw-infer/api/v1/generate --env SAMPLE_RATE=0.05
- Prometheus scrape query snapshot exported to artifacts/perf/2026-02-11/prom-snapshot.json

Detailed observations
- KV priming: We see a sharp window where kv_prime_ops_total spikes, then a sustained elevated request latency until the KV cache stabilizes. The client-sample-driven priming at 0.05 was insufficient to prime hot keys across the pool.
- Warmup CPU behavior: host-level context-switches correlate tightly with the long-sequence requests; when priming was done in parallel with inference work, we saw CPU saturation leading to queueing delays. Serial priming reduced CPU contention but extended warmup time.
- Allocator effects: reverting the allocator tweak reduced the number of 1–2s stalls that were visible in traces; these stalls line up with dynamic memory compaction ops in the new allocator.

Decisions made in the meeting
- Short-term (hotfix-able in next 48–72h):
  - Increase default client sample_rate for mixed workloads from 0.05 -> 0.15 for the hosted API (config toggle + rollout via feature flag). Owner: Ethan P. Target: 2026-02-15
  - Add server-side prepopulate hook as an optional warmup flag for heavy mixed workloads; enable only for dedicated pools where CPU headroom exists. Owner: Marisol V. Target: 2026-02-18
- Mid-term (next sprint):
  - Revert allocator change in the mainline and run a full battery of stress runs with the quant kernels; engage release-engineering to produce a canary. Owner: Ravi I. Target: 2026-02-26
  - Implement a controlled rollout for kernel v2.3.1 that throttles priming and staggers instance warmup windows to avoid synchronized warmup spikes. Owner: SRE/AutoScaling (Tom H.). Target: 2026-03-04
- Long-term:
  - Investigate a KV-priming strategy that uses lightweight sampling + selective priming of top-n keys per model bucket (research item). Owner: Priya D. Target: 2026-Q2

Action items (compact)
- Ethan: flip sample_rate feature flag to 0.15 on staging and run mixed_chat stress test (due 2026-02-15).
- Marisol: PR for server-side prepopulate hook and config knob; include CPU guard rail (due 2026-02-18). (GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8912 referenced)
- Ravi: prepare revert patch for allocator and schedule canary (due 2026-02-20).
- Tom: proposal for staggered warmup windows, include rollout playbook (due 2026-02-19).
- Priya: draft research scope for selective-KV priming and add to Optimize backlog (due 2026-02-28).

Notes for validation and follow-up
- Validation criteria for hotfix: p99 within 10% of baseline on 30m mixed_chat run at 1200 qps and stable token throughput.
- Observability checklist: ensure kv_prime_ops_total and kv_cache_hit_ratio are exported per-instance and that traces during warmup have higher sample rate (1:50) for first 3 mins.
- Track rollouts using tag: perf-warmup-feb2026 in deployments and correlate with incidents.

Appendix (raw sample numbers)
- baseline-2026-02-02: qps 1200, p50 28ms, p95 62ms, p99 114ms
- reg-2026-02-11: qps 1200, p50 30ms, p95 68ms, p99 132ms
- run-A-2026-02-12: qps 1200, p99 116ms
- run-C-2026-02-12: qps 1200, p99 118ms
- run-D-2026-02-13: qps 1200, p99 120ms

If anything missing or you have additional telemetry to share (prom snapshots, raw traces), paste links into the Jira ticket SERV-4122 and tag the run ID so we can replay the exact sequence.

End of notes.
